recovered_source_fields.action_description:
此验证动作还原了验证机器人利用 Powershell 加载的不安全库来加载易受攻击的 amsi.dll 版本，以绕过反恶意软件扫描接口 (AMSI)。成功执行后，powershell.exe 将被复制并重命名为 updater.exe，并从非标准路径加载 amsi.dll。

劫持 DLL 加载可能是为了建立持久化以及提升权限和/或规避文件执行的限制。
recovered_source_fields.action_name: Host command line - evasion Anti-Malware Scan Interface
recovered_source_fields.validation_rule_raw_text:
copy %windir%\System32\windowspowershell\v1.0\powershell.exe /Y %APPDATA%\updater.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

copy %windir%\System32\amsi.dll /Y %APPDATA%\amsi.dll
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

start %APPDATA%\updater.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

tasklist
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:updater.exe

#Cleanup
taskkill /F /IM updater.exe
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

del %APPDATA%\updater.exe >nul 2>&1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

del %APPDATA%\amsi.dll >nul 2>&1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the use of unsafe libraries loaded by Powershell by the Validator to load vulnerable versions of amsi.dll, evasioning the Anti Malware Scanning Interface (AMSI). After successful execution, powershell.exe will be copied and renamed as updater.exe, and amsi.dll will be loaded from a non-standard path. Hijacking DLL loading may be done to establish persistence, elevate permissions, and/or circumvent restrictions on file execution.

  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

start %APPDATA%\updater.exe
  auto,4,true,60
  success_zero

tasklist
  auto,4,true,60
  success_match:updater.exe

#Cleanup
taskkill /F /IM updater.exe
  auto,4,true,3

del %APPDATA%\updater.exe >nul 2>&1
  auto,4,true,3
  cleanup

del %APPDATA%\amsi.dll >nul 2>&1
  auto,4,true,3

此验证动作使用 reg query 来查询注册表项“HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Nls\Language”。 KeyName 返回的十六进制值 InstallLanguage 表示 Windows 区域设置 ID。每个 ID 对应一个使用相同语言的区域。

注意：此验证动作被视为“弱信号”操作。这意味着它展示的行为并不总是表示恶意活动，并且可以匹配合法用户或管理活动。当您单独运行弱信号操作时，它不太可能被安全产品阻止。最佳实践是确保您的安全产品提供对此类行为的可见性。这使您可以将活动与更高保真度的信号关联起来以进行检测或用于威胁搜寻。

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the installed language used by the host operating system as determined by adversary. Adversary sometimes uses this information to attempt to determine the area where the target computer is located. This validation rule uses a reg query to query the registry key "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Nls\Language". The hexadecimal value InstallLanguage returned by KeyName represents the Windows Locale ID. Each ID corresponds to a region that uses the same language. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious campaign and can match legitimate users or manage campaigns. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by Security Controls. The best practice is to ensure that your Security Controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat search.

exact_source_fields.notes: Digidations recommends running this rule as a SYSTEM, non-administrator, or administrator user on Windows Server 2016, Windows 10, or Windows 7 Validator.

exact_source_fields.desc: This validation rule simulates the installed language used by the host operating system as determined by adversary. Adversary sometimes uses this information to attempt to determine the area where the target computer is located. This validation rule uses a reg query to query the registry key "HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Nls\Language". The hexadecimal value InstallLanguage returned by KeyName represents the Windows Locale ID. Each ID corresponds to a region that uses the same language. Note: This validation rule is considered a "weak signal" operation. This means that the behavior it displays does not always indicate malicious campaign and can match legitimate users or manage campaigns. When you run a weak signal operation alone, it is unlikely to be blocked by Security Controls. The best practice is to ensure that your Security Controls provide visibility into such behavior. This allows you to associate campaigns with higher fidelity signals for detection or for threat search.
